description:
Advances: ancora.parsing

Ancora 1.0 cannot represent a subject pruned under an authorizing ADR. append_only.ex:82 authorizes a requirement deletion only when the accepted ADR's affects: names the deleted requirement id or its subject id, while DecisionParser.Affects resolves affects: strictly against the CURRENT index — a pruned subject and its requirement ids are gone from that index by definition, so the same ADR that satisfies the append-only guard emits adr/affects_unresolved at error, persistently, on every future spec.validate run. No corpus shape satisfies both rules. This is a spec-design gap, not a code bug: ancora.parsing's requirement (that an affects id not in the corpus shall emit adr/affects_unresolved) mandates the behavior, so the fix is a spec edit with clause accounting plus implementation — e.g. a retires:/retired-affects vocabulary the resolver exempts and the append-only guard accepts as authorization — and a 1.0.x release.

Surfaced by the M7 Engage migration (ancora-yzu.23), which prunes spec.system under its migration ADR. Interim posture consumers carry until this lands: severities adr/affects_unresolved: info in the consumer config, recorded in the migration ADR (trailers cannot price it — the finding is persistent, trailers are commit-scoped). Consumers that took the demotion should re-tighten to the registry default when adopting the release that closes this ticket. Not an epic child: the demotion unblocks all remaining migrations (M7-M9), so nothing in ancora-yzu depends on this fix.

Status note (2026-09-03): the 'Not an epic child' sentence above predates this ticket being re-homed under ancora-xla. It is a child now. Blocked by ancora-v1n because both tickets redefine what an ADR affects: entry authorizes; the retirement vocabulary must be built on the authorization rule v1n settles.

Ruling needed before code moves (Manuel): what vocabulary lets an accepted ADR name a retired subject or requirement id so that cold spec.validate accepts it and the append-only guard treats it as authorization?
Recommended default from the ticket: a retires: field on the ADR (alongside affects:) whose ids the Affects resolver exempts from adr/affects_unresolved and which append_only.ex accepts as authorization for the named deletions. Requires a new must in ancora.parsing with clause accounting, and a 1.0.x release note.
Worker: if no comment on this ticket records a ruling when you start, park and ask. Do not choose on Manuel's behalf and do not implement more than one option.

Verification:
- Tests to pass: tagged tests for the new ancora.parsing requirement plus existing tags under ancora.parsing for affects resolution and append-only authorization (test/ancora/decision_parser_test.exs, test/ancora/append_only_test.exs)
- Behaviors to demonstrate: (1) a corpus that deletes a whole subject under an accepted ADR naming it in the retirement vocabulary passes mix spec.validate cold with zero adr/affects_unresolved and zero append/requirement_deleted; (2) an id that is neither in the index nor in the retirement vocabulary still emits adr/affects_unresolved at error; (3) the vocabulary appears in the spec.init decision template so new adopters see it
- Verification cadence:
  - Iteration tier: mix test --stale or explicitly named test files, plus mix spec.validate; no full suite mid-iteration.
  - Final tier: immediately before IMPLEMENTED, run-until-green: mix compile --warnings-as-errors && mix test && mix format --check-formatted && mix deps.unlock --check-unused && mix spec.check --base the epic base sha recorded at admission
  - Verifier tier: mix spec.check --base the epic base sha recorded at admission plus tagged and --stale selections only; do NOT run the full suite.
- Standing bounce-class checks:
  - Production call site named for each new callable surface, with the proving test that exercises that production path.
  - Fixture hygiene: one TmpGitRepo per test, no shared temp dirs, async only where the fixture allows.
  - Spec surfaces kept fresh for every touched callable surface. Drift, growth, and shrink clear only through substantive requirement or scenario edits in the same diff, never through a Spec-Ack trailer.
  - Every conditional clause covered by a test.
- proves: a pruned subject under an authorizing ADR validates clean without any severity demotion or tombstone files.

Allowed touches (this ticket may modify):
- lib/ancora/append_only.ex
- lib/ancora/decision_parser.ex
- lib/ancora/decision_parser/affects.ex
- lib/ancora/schema/decision.ex
- test/ancora/append_only_test.exs
- test/ancora/decision_parser_test.exs
- test/support/**
- .spec/specs/ancora.parsing.spec.md (new requirement plus clause accounting for the affects_unresolved must; substantive edits, not a trailer)
- .spec/decisions/** (the ADR recording the vocabulary)
- priv/spec_init/decisions/** and test/ancora/scaffold/templates_test.exs (decision template gains the field)
- docs/migration.md, README.md (document the field and tell Engage/Builder consumers how to retire their interim posture)

Out of Scope (files):
- lib/ancora/gate*
- lib/ancora/derive/**
- lib/ancora/review/**
- lib/mix/tasks/**
- lib/ancora/output*

Out of Scope (intent):
- no change to how affects: resolves for ids that ARE in the index
- no repo-wide severity demotion as the fix; the consumer demotions are the interim posture this ticket retires
- no git-history lookup inside spec.validate; the vocabulary lives in the corpus

Merge gate:
- [ ] mix compile --warnings-as-errors
- [ ] mix test
- [ ] mix format --check-formatted
- [ ] mix deps.unlock --check-unused
- [ ] mix spec.check --base the epic base sha recorded at admission ends result=pass
- [ ] Scope check: diff touches only Allowed globs (mechanical)
- [ ] Auditor APPROVE comment on the ticket

comments.text:
Second consumer hit this gap within hours: Builder (ancora-yzu.24) chose the OTHER interim shape — six metadata-only identifier tombstone files kept so the retirement ADR affects: resolves, with scoped unanchored-subject overrides — where Engage (ancora-yzu.23) took the repo-wide severities demotion adr/affects_unresolved: info. Both are recorded in their migration ADRs with pointers here. When this ticket lands: Engage re-tightens the demotion to the registry default, Builder deletes the six tombstones (its completion record names them). Design input from the field: the fix must let spec.validate (cold, no git) accept an accepted ADR naming retired ids — resolving against base-at-PR-time is not available to validate, so the vocabulary likely needs to live in the corpus (e.g. a retires: field the resolver exempts and the append-only guard accepts as authorization).

Session: 68fab1f9-dfb5-49e0-be76-afa9d2d00f6d
Log: /Users/mz/.claude-personal/projects/-Users-mz-src-ancora/68fab1f9-dfb5-49e0-be76-afa9d2d00f6d.jsonl

RULING (Manuel, 2026-09-03): Option A. Add a retires: field on the ADR next to affects:. The Affects resolver exempts ids listed there from adr/affects_unresolved, and the append-only guard accepts them as authorization for the named deletions. A subject id in retires: covers every requirement under it, so pruning a whole subject does not require listing each requirement (this is the shorthand the v1n ruling leaves room for). No registry file, no new spec block type. Update the Zoi decision schema, the spec.init decision template, docs/migration.md, and write the unwind note: Engage re-tightens adr/affects_unresolved to the registry default, Builder deletes its six tombstone files.

title: Retirement vocabulary for ADR affects: (subject-pruning catch-22)
